OpenSubs is a browser tool that transcribes speech into subtitles, translates them, styles them, and burns them into a video. This page describes exactly what data the tool collects, what it never collects, and why. The OpenSubs app is open source (AGPL-3.0-or-later), so what it does with your files can be checked in its code.
OpenSubs is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect information from them.

OpenSubs lets you burn subtitles into video here, in the tab. The video is read straight off your disk, libass draws the subtitles exactly as the preview showed them, and WebCodecs encodes the result to MP4 with the audio copied across untouched rather than re-encoded. There is no upload step, because there is no server to upload to — which is also why there is no file-size cap, no queue and no watermark.

The subtitle generator as a command-line tool: one command per file, for scripting and for CI. Same engine, same presets, same output. Build it from source; it needs an ffmpeg built with the ass filter (libass).

The subtitle generator needs a browser with WebAssembly: Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox. WebGPU makes transcription faster but is not required. The speech model is downloaded once, about 40 to 250 MB depending on the size you pick, and then cached by the browser. iOS 17 Safari cannot run the recogniser; iOS 26 works.

The subtitle generator on macOS, Windows and Linux, for long files. The macOS and Windows installers include ffmpeg; on Linux, install one built with the ass filter (libass). On Windows it is also on the Microsoft Store; the builds on GitHub are unsigned.

The subtitle generator runs OpenAI's Whisper locally — ONNX weights driven by transformers.js, on WebGPU where the machine has it and on WebAssembly otherwise. Three model sizes are offered: Tiny (English only, about 40 MB), Base (about 80 MB) and Small (about 250 MB).
